brief: Oil surged on Middle East escalation and the shutdown of Saudi Arabia's 7m b/d East-West pipeline. ICE Brent hit an intraday high just below $110/bbl before front-month futures settled over 1% higher at $105.68/bbl, following Trump's comments that Iran is open to a deal and Russia and Ukraine agreed to stop hitting each other's energy infrastructure. Despite that agreement, gasoil cracks held above $80/bbl near record levels, which the note reads as market skepticism, and Russia's diesel export ban runs through month-end, keeping US export-control talk alive even as the administration argues a ban would do little to cut prices now but would raise refinery costs and prices later. European gas stays supported on weak Gulf LNG hopes and EU storage at 68% versus an 84% seasonal average. Gold fell as the oil-driven inflation scare firmed odds of the Fed's first hike since 2023 this week, though much of that is priced in. Copper fell on AI-slowdown concerns for data-centre demand plus easing exchange tightness, even as mine-supply constraints should keep supporting prices. China has bought about 13mt of its 25mt soybean commitment ahead of Xi's Washington visit. Ukraine's 2026/27 grain exports are down 24% year-on-year on Black Sea attacks.
